messages.author: Daniel Konstantinovsky
messages.body:
Hello Amber,
I want to use tleap to solvate a protein but I want to keep the
crystallographic water molecules in place as regular solvent but with their
initial positions. I have added hydrogens to these waters and made them
TIP4P by adding an EPW dummy atom. I checked and it seems tleap strips the
water molecules off the structure before/while solvating because none of
the new water molecules have the coordinates of any of the original waters.
Some of the water molecules are in hidden pockets of the protein that the
solvent would never penetrate in a reasonable amount of time. What can I do?
Thank you!
Dan

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
If you just leave them as found and named in the pdb file it should work
fine (if it's from RCSB). If it doesn't work, share the leap.log so we can
see what leap did.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Thu, Mar 10, 2022, Daniel Konstantinovsky wrote:
>
>I want to use tleap to solvate a protein but I want to keep the
>crystallographic water molecules in place as regular solvent but with their
>initial positions. I have added hydrogens to these waters and made them
>TIP4P by adding an EPW dummy atom. I checked and it seems tleap strips the
>water molecules off the structure....
This is unlikely: tleap doesn't remove waters (or anything else). There
should be no need to add hydrogens or add dummy atoms: if they are called
HOH or WAT, they should get recognized, and whatever force field you
requested in your leaprc.water.xxxx will be applied. (You might try
renaming the crystallographic waters as WAT, but I don't think(?) that
should be needed.)
Look carefully at the leap.log file for any clues about what is happening.
You might post the relevant parts of the PDB file, and the tleap commands to
you are using.
...good luck...dac

messages.author: Daniel Konstantinovsky
messages.body:
I think all that is happening is that tleap translates the system to a new
center. I have confirmed that the original waters are still there by
aligning to the original structure. I'm just writing this for future people
who have this problem so they see that it's ok.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Mar 11, 2022, Daniel Konstantinovsky wrote:
>I think all that is happening is that tleap translates the system to a new
>center. I have confirmed that the original waters are still there by
>aligning to the original structure. I'm just writing this for future people
>who have this problem so they see that it's ok.
Good catch. You can disable such behavior by issuing a "set default
nocenter on" command to tleap before doing anything that creates a periodic
system.
....dac
